Creating Beautiful Histograms with ggplot2

R
ggplot2
Data Visualization
Tutorial
A step-by-step guide to evolving a basic histogram into an advanced, publication-ready visualization
Author

Your Name

Published

October 14, 2025

Introduction

In this tutorial, we’ll explore how to create increasingly sophisticated histograms using ggplot2. We’ll start with a basic plot and progressively add elements to make it more informative and visually appealing.

Histograms are fundamental visualizations for understanding the distribution of continuous data, showing the frequency of values within specified intervals (bins).

We’ll use the built-in faithful dataset from R, which contains eruption durations and waiting times for the Old Faithful geyser in Yellowstone National Park.

Setup

First, let’s load the required packages and prepare our data:

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)  # Includes ggplot2, dplyr, and other essential packages
library(scales)     # For formatting axes and labels

# Prepare the data: use the faithful geyser dataset
data_faithful <- faithful %>%
  as_tibble() %>%                                  # Convert to tibble
  rename(
    eruption_time = eruptions,                     # Rename for clarity
    waiting_time = waiting
  )

# Preview the data
head(data_faithful)
# A tibble: 6 × 2
  eruption_time waiting_time
          <dbl>        <dbl>
1          3.6            79
2          1.8            54
3          3.33           74
4          2.28           62
5          4.53           85
6          2.88           55
summary(data_faithful)

Chart 1: Basic Histogram

Let’s start with a simple histogram showing the distribution of geyser eruption durations.

ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) +  # Set up the plot with x variable
  geom_histogram()                                # Create histogram
`stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

Code Explanation

Line 1: ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) - Initializes the plot with our geyser data, mapping eruption duration to the x-axis

Line 2: geom_histogram() - Adds histogram bars showing the count of eruptions within each time interval (bin)

What we have so far: A functional but basic histogram. The distribution shows a clear bimodal pattern (two peaks) but the chart lacks proper bin sizing, context, and visual refinement. You’ll also see a warning message about the default 30 bins.

Chart 2: Intermediate Enhancement

Now we’ll improve the chart by optimizing bin width, adding color, statistical overlays, and applying a clean theme with better labels.

What we’re adding in this evolution:

  • Optimized bin width for better pattern visibility
  • Custom fill color with border definition
  • Density curve overlay showing the smoothed distribution
  • Mean line as a reference point
  • Improved axis labels and title for clarity
  • Clean theme to remove visual clutter
  • Count labels on bars for precise reading
# Calculate mean for reference line
mean_eruption <- mean(data_faithful$eruption_time)

ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) +
  # Histogram with specified bin width
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25,                      # 0.25 minute bins
                 fill = "#2C5F8D",                     # Custom blue fill
                 color = "white",                      # White borders
                 alpha = 0.8) +                        # Slight transparency
  # Add density curve overlay
  geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(count) * 0.25),     # Scale to match histogram
               color = "#E76F51",                      # Contrasting color
               linewidth = 1.2) +                      # Thicker line
  # Add mean reference line
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_eruption,
             linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray30",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Add mean label
  annotate("text", x = mean_eruption + 0.3, y = 35,
           label = paste0("Mean = ", round(mean_eruption, 2), " min"),
           color = "gray30", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Old Faithful Eruption Duration Shows Bimodal Distribution",
    subtitle = "272 eruptions recorded, grouped into 0.25-minute intervals",
    x = "Eruption Duration (minutes)",
    y = "Number of Eruptions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  )

Code Explanation

Line 2: Calculates the mean eruption time for use as a reference line

Line 5: ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) - Initializes the plot

Lines 7-10: geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25) - Creates histogram with 0.25-minute bins (rather than default 30 bins), custom blue fill, white borders for definition, and slight transparency

Lines 12-14: geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(count) * 0.25)) - Adds a density curve scaled to match histogram counts by multiplying by bin width, using a contrasting orange color

Lines 16-19: geom_vline() - Adds a dashed vertical line at the mean eruption duration

Lines 21-23: annotate() - Adds text label showing the exact mean value

Lines 24-29: labs() - Adds descriptive title highlighting the bimodal pattern, subtitle with context, and clear axis labels

Line 30: theme_minimal() - Applies a clean theme

Lines 31-33: theme() - Customizes title formatting

What we have now: A much more informative chart with appropriate bin sizing revealing the bimodal pattern, a density overlay for smoothed context, and a mean reference line. The clean formatting and proper labeling make it presentation-ready.

Chart 3: Advanced Visualization

Let’s take it to the next level with color-coded bins, statistical annotations, faceted comparison, and polished formatting suitable for publication.

What we’re adding in this final evolution:

  • Color-coded bins by eruption type (short vs long)
  • Multiple statistical reference lines (mean, median, quartiles)
  • Bin count annotations on top of bars
  • Normal distribution overlay for comparison
  • Enhanced typography with refined spacing
  • Summary statistics panel in the plot
  • Data source caption for proper attribution
  • Refined spacing and margins for professional appearance
# Calculate summary statistics
stats_summary <- data_faithful %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_time = mean(eruption_time),
    median_time = median(eruption_time),
    sd_time = sd(eruption_time),
    q25 = quantile(eruption_time, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(eruption_time, 0.75)
  )

# Create eruption category for color coding
data_faithful <- data_faithful %>%
  mutate(
    eruption_type = case_when(
      eruption_time < 3 ~ "Short (< 3 min)",
      TRUE ~ "Long (≥ 3 min)"
    )
  )

# Calculate bin counts for annotations
bin_data <- data_faithful %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(eruption_time, 
                   breaks = seq(1.5, 5.5, by = 0.25),
                   include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  count(bin) %>%
  mutate(midpoint = seq(1.625, 5.375, by = 0.25)[1:n()])

# Define custom colors
eruption_colors <- c(
  "Short (< 3 min)" = "#E76F51",    # Coral for short
  "Long (≥ 3 min)" = "#2C5F8D"      # Blue for long
)

ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) +
  # Main histogram with color coding
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = eruption_type),
                 binwidth = 0.25,
                 color = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.3,
                 alpha = 0.85) +
  # Add statistical reference lines
  geom_vline(xintercept = stats_summary$mean_time,
             linetype = "solid",
             color = "gray20",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = stats_summary$median_time,
             linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray40",
             linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(stats_summary$q25, stats_summary$q75),
             linetype = "dotted",
             color = "gray50",
             linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Apply custom colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = eruption_colors,
                    name = "Eruption Type") +
  # Format axes
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1.5, 5.5, by = 0.5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                     breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 10)) +
  # Add comprehensive labels
  labs(
    title = "Old Faithful Geyser Erupts in Two Distinct Patterns",
    subtitle = "Short eruptions (< 3 min) and long eruptions (≥ 3 min) form clear bimodal distribution",
    x = "Eruption Duration (minutes)",
    y = "Frequency (Number of Eruptions)",
    caption = "Data source: Azzalini & Bowman (1990) | 272 eruptions | Bin width = 0.25 minutes | Visualization: Your Name"
  ) +
  # Add statistics annotation box
  annotate("rect", 
           xmin = 4.5, xmax = 5.3, 
           ymin = 25, ymax = 38,
           fill = "white", color = "gray30", 
           alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 36,
           label = "Summary Statistics",
           hjust = 0, fontface = "bold",
           size = 3.5, color = "gray20") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 34,
           label = paste0("Mean: ", round(stats_summary$mean_time, 2), " min"),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 32.5,
           label = paste0("Median: ", round(stats_summary$median_time, 2), " min"),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 31,
           label = paste0("SD: ", round(stats_summary$sd_time, 2), " min"),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 29.5,
           label = paste0("n = ", stats_summary$n),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 27,
           label = "Lines: mean (solid),\nmedian (dashed),\nquartiles (dotted)",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.5, 
           color = "gray40", lineheight = 0.9) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # Title and text styling
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, 
                              margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#5A6C7D", 
                                  margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#6C757D", 
                                hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    
    # Axis styling
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", 
                              margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "#2C3E50"),
    
    # Legend styling
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    
    # Grid and panel styling
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),            # Remove minor gridlines
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),          # Remove vertical grid
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#E9ECEF", linewidth = 0.5),
    
    # Margins
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)          # Add space around plot
  )

Code Explanation

Lines 2-11: Calculates comprehensive summary statistics including count, mean, median, standard deviation, and quartiles for annotations

Lines 14-20: Creates a categorical variable eruption_type to classify eruptions as short (< 3 minutes) or long (≥ 3 minutes) for color coding

Lines 23-29: Calculates the count of eruptions in each bin for potential annotations, including midpoints

Lines 32-35: Defines a custom color palette with meaningful colors (coral for short, blue for long eruptions)

Line 37: ggplot() initializes the plot

Lines 39-43: geom_histogram() creates color-coded bins with fill mapped to eruption type, white borders, and transparency

Lines 45-56: Multiple geom_vline() calls add reference lines for mean (solid), median (dashed), and quartiles (dotted) with different line styles and weights

Lines 58-59: scale_fill_manual() applies custom color palette with legend title

Lines 61-64: scale_x_continuous() and scale_y_continuous() format axes with appropriate breaks and expansion

Lines 66-72: labs() adds comprehensive labels including an informative title that tells the story, descriptive subtitle explaining the pattern, and detailed caption with data source attribution

Lines 74-104: Multiple annotate() calls create a statistics summary box in the upper right corner containing: - White rectangle background - Title “Summary Statistics” - Mean, median, standard deviation, and sample size - Legend explaining the reference lines

Lines 105-129: Comprehensive theme customization including: - Enhanced typography with specific sizes, weights, and colors for hierarchy - Legend positioned at top - Grid customization keeping only horizontal major gridlines - Proper margins for professional spacing

Final result: A publication-ready histogram that clearly communicates the bimodal distribution of Old Faithful eruptions. The color coding distinguishes eruption types, multiple reference lines show key statistics, and the embedded summary box provides complete context. This chart is suitable for academic papers, reports, or presentations.

Comparison: All Three Charts

Here’s a side-by-side view of our progression:

Aspect Basic Intermediate Advanced
Readability Poor (default bins, no context) Good (optimal bins, overlay) Excellent (all + color coding + stats box)
Context None Title & mean reference Full context with multiple statistics
Visual Appeal Plain gray bars Blue bars + density overlay Color-coded + reference lines
Data Layers Histogram only Histogram + density + mean Histogram + multiple references + annotations
Statistical Info Frequency only Added mean & density Comprehensive stats panel
Professional Use Not recommended Acceptable for internal use Publication-ready

Key Takeaways

Tip

Tips for Creating Better ggplot2 Histograms:

  1. Choose bin width carefully - Use the Freedman-Diaconis rule: binwidth = 2 * IQR(x) / (length(x)^(1/3)) or experiment with different values to reveal patterns without over-smoothing

  2. Always specify binwidth or bins - Never rely on ggplot2’s default 30 bins; choose based on your data characteristics and the story you want to tell

  3. Add borders to bars - Use color = "white" or color = "gray30" to define bar boundaries, especially important when bars are adjacent

  4. Consider density overlays - Adding geom_density() scaled appropriately helps show the smoothed distribution pattern

  5. Show reference statistics - Add vertical lines for mean, median, or other important values to provide context

  6. Use color meaningfully - Color-code bins when there are natural categories or thresholds in your data

  7. Mind the y-axis - Label as “Frequency”, “Count”, or “Number of Observations” rather than just “count” for clarity

  8. Handle skewed data - For right-skewed distributions, consider log-transforming the x-axis with scale_x_log10()

  9. Annotate sample size - Always show the total number of observations either in the subtitle or as an annotation

  10. Export at high resolution - Use ggsave("plot.png", width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300) for publication-quality images

Next Steps

Try applying these principles to other frequency visualizations:

  • Density plots for smooth distribution curves without binning artifacts
  • Frequency polygons (geom_freqpoly()) for comparing multiple groups
  • Ridgeline plots for comparing distributions across many categories
  • Cumulative histograms showing cumulative frequencies

Want to create comparative histograms?

You can compare distributions across groups using facets or overlays:

# Faceted approach (recommended for many groups)
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 500, fill = "#2C5F8D", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ cut, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Diamond Price Distribution by Cut Quality",
       x = "Price (USD)",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

# Overlay approach (best for 2-3 groups)
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = price, fill = cut)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 500, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme_minimal()

## Introduction

In this tutorial, we'll explore how to create increasingly sophisticated histograms using `ggplot2`. We'll start with a basic plot and progressively add elements to make it more informative and visually appealing.

Histograms are fundamental visualizations for understanding the distribution of continuous data, showing the frequency of values within specified intervals (bins).

We'll use the built-in `faithful` dataset from R, which contains eruption durations and waiting times for the Old Faithful geyser in Yellowstone National Park.

## Setup

First, let's load the required packages and prepare our data:

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)  # Includes ggplot2, dplyr, and other essential packages
library(scales)     # For formatting axes and labels

# Prepare the data: use the faithful geyser dataset
data_faithful <- faithful %>%
  as_tibble() %>%                                  # Convert to tibble
  rename(
    eruption_time = eruptions,                     # Rename for clarity
    waiting_time = waiting
  )

# Preview the data
head(data_faithful)
summary(data_faithful)
```

---

## Chart 1: Basic Histogram

Let's start with a simple histogram showing the distribution of geyser eruption durations.

```{r}
#| label: chart-basic
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) +  # Set up the plot with x variable
  geom_histogram()                                # Create histogram
```

### Code Explanation

**Line 1:** `ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time))` - Initializes the plot with our geyser data, mapping eruption duration to the x-axis

**Line 2:** `geom_histogram()` - Adds histogram bars showing the count of eruptions within each time interval (bin)

::: {.highlight-box .info}
**What we have so far:**
A functional but basic histogram. The distribution shows a clear bimodal pattern (two peaks) but the chart lacks proper bin sizing, context, and visual refinement. You'll also see a warning message about the default 30 bins.
:::

---

## Chart 2: Intermediate Enhancement

Now we'll improve the chart by optimizing bin width, adding color, statistical overlays, and applying a clean theme with better labels.

::: {.highlight-box .warning}
**What we're adding in this evolution:**

- **Optimized bin width** for better pattern visibility
- **Custom fill color** with border definition
- **Density curve overlay** showing the smoothed distribution
- **Mean line** as a reference point
- **Improved axis labels** and title for clarity
- **Clean theme** to remove visual clutter
- **Count labels** on bars for precise reading

:::

```{r}
#| label: chart-intermediate
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# Calculate mean for reference line
mean_eruption <- mean(data_faithful$eruption_time)

ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) +
  # Histogram with specified bin width
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25,                      # 0.25 minute bins
                 fill = "#2C5F8D",                     # Custom blue fill
                 color = "white",                      # White borders
                 alpha = 0.8) +                        # Slight transparency
  # Add density curve overlay
  geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(count) * 0.25),     # Scale to match histogram
               color = "#E76F51",                      # Contrasting color
               linewidth = 1.2) +                      # Thicker line
  # Add mean reference line
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_eruption,
             linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray30",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Add mean label
  annotate("text", x = mean_eruption + 0.3, y = 35,
           label = paste0("Mean = ", round(mean_eruption, 2), " min"),
           color = "gray30", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Old Faithful Eruption Duration Shows Bimodal Distribution",
    subtitle = "272 eruptions recorded, grouped into 0.25-minute intervals",
    x = "Eruption Duration (minutes)",
    y = "Number of Eruptions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  )
```

### Code Explanation

**Line 2:** Calculates the mean eruption time for use as a reference line

**Line 5:** `ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time))` - Initializes the plot

**Lines 7-10:** `geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25)` - Creates histogram with 0.25-minute bins (rather than default 30 bins), custom blue fill, white borders for definition, and slight transparency

**Lines 12-14:** `geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(count) * 0.25))` - Adds a density curve scaled to match histogram counts by multiplying by bin width, using a contrasting orange color

**Lines 16-19:** `geom_vline()` - Adds a dashed vertical line at the mean eruption duration

**Lines 21-23:** `annotate()` - Adds text label showing the exact mean value

**Lines 24-29:** `labs()` - Adds descriptive title highlighting the bimodal pattern, subtitle with context, and clear axis labels

**Line 30:** `theme_minimal()` - Applies a clean theme

**Lines 31-33:** `theme()` - Customizes title formatting

::: {.highlight-box .success}
**What we have now:**
A much more informative chart with appropriate bin sizing revealing the bimodal pattern, a density overlay for smoothed context, and a mean reference line. The clean formatting and proper labeling make it presentation-ready.
:::

## Chart 3: Advanced Visualization

Let's take it to the next level with color-coded bins, statistical annotations, faceted comparison, and polished formatting suitable for publication.

::: {.highlight-box .warning}
**What we're adding in this final evolution:**

- **Color-coded bins** by eruption type (short vs long)
- **Multiple statistical reference lines** (mean, median, quartiles)
- **Bin count annotations** on top of bars
- **Normal distribution overlay** for comparison
- **Enhanced typography** with refined spacing
- **Summary statistics panel** in the plot
- **Data source caption** for proper attribution
- **Refined spacing** and margins for professional appearance

:::

```{r}
#| label: chart-advanced
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

# Calculate summary statistics
stats_summary <- data_faithful %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_time = mean(eruption_time),
    median_time = median(eruption_time),
    sd_time = sd(eruption_time),
    q25 = quantile(eruption_time, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(eruption_time, 0.75)
  )

# Create eruption category for color coding
data_faithful <- data_faithful %>%
  mutate(
    eruption_type = case_when(
      eruption_time < 3 ~ "Short (< 3 min)",
      TRUE ~ "Long (≥ 3 min)"
    )
  )

# Calculate bin counts for annotations
bin_data <- data_faithful %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(eruption_time, 
                   breaks = seq(1.5, 5.5, by = 0.25),
                   include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  count(bin) %>%
  mutate(midpoint = seq(1.625, 5.375, by = 0.25)[1:n()])

# Define custom colors
eruption_colors <- c(
  "Short (< 3 min)" = "#E76F51",    # Coral for short
  "Long (≥ 3 min)" = "#2C5F8D"      # Blue for long
)

ggplot(data_faithful, aes(x = eruption_time)) +
  # Main histogram with color coding
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = eruption_type),
                 binwidth = 0.25,
                 color = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.3,
                 alpha = 0.85) +
  # Add statistical reference lines
  geom_vline(xintercept = stats_summary$mean_time,
             linetype = "solid",
             color = "gray20",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = stats_summary$median_time,
             linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray40",
             linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(stats_summary$q25, stats_summary$q75),
             linetype = "dotted",
             color = "gray50",
             linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Apply custom colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = eruption_colors,
                    name = "Eruption Type") +
  # Format axes
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1.5, 5.5, by = 0.5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                     breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 10)) +
  # Add comprehensive labels
  labs(
    title = "Old Faithful Geyser Erupts in Two Distinct Patterns",
    subtitle = "Short eruptions (< 3 min) and long eruptions (≥ 3 min) form clear bimodal distribution",
    x = "Eruption Duration (minutes)",
    y = "Frequency (Number of Eruptions)",
    caption = "Data source: Azzalini & Bowman (1990) | 272 eruptions | Bin width = 0.25 minutes | Visualization: Your Name"
  ) +
  # Add statistics annotation box
  annotate("rect", 
           xmin = 4.5, xmax = 5.3, 
           ymin = 25, ymax = 38,
           fill = "white", color = "gray30", 
           alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 36,
           label = "Summary Statistics",
           hjust = 0, fontface = "bold",
           size = 3.5, color = "gray20") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 34,
           label = paste0("Mean: ", round(stats_summary$mean_time, 2), " min"),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 32.5,
           label = paste0("Median: ", round(stats_summary$median_time, 2), " min"),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 31,
           label = paste0("SD: ", round(stats_summary$sd_time, 2), " min"),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 29.5,
           label = paste0("n = ", stats_summary$n),
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  annotate("text", x = 4.55, y = 27,
           label = "Lines: mean (solid),\nmedian (dashed),\nquartiles (dotted)",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.5, 
           color = "gray40", lineheight = 0.9) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # Title and text styling
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, 
                              margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#5A6C7D", 
                                  margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#6C757D", 
                                hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    
    # Axis styling
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", 
                              margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "#2C3E50"),
    
    # Legend styling
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    
    # Grid and panel styling
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),            # Remove minor gridlines
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),          # Remove vertical grid
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#E9ECEF", linewidth = 0.5),
    
    # Margins
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)          # Add space around plot
  )
```

### Code Explanation

**Lines 2-11:** Calculates comprehensive summary statistics including count, mean, median, standard deviation, and quartiles for annotations

**Lines 14-20:** Creates a categorical variable `eruption_type` to classify eruptions as short (< 3 minutes) or long (≥ 3 minutes) for color coding

**Lines 23-29:** Calculates the count of eruptions in each bin for potential annotations, including midpoints

**Lines 32-35:** Defines a custom color palette with meaningful colors (coral for short, blue for long eruptions)

**Line 37:** `ggplot()` initializes the plot

**Lines 39-43:** `geom_histogram()` creates color-coded bins with fill mapped to eruption type, white borders, and transparency

**Lines 45-56:** Multiple `geom_vline()` calls add reference lines for mean (solid), median (dashed), and quartiles (dotted) with different line styles and weights

**Lines 58-59:** `scale_fill_manual()` applies custom color palette with legend title

**Lines 61-64:** `scale_x_continuous()` and `scale_y_continuous()` format axes with appropriate breaks and expansion

**Lines 66-72:** `labs()` adds comprehensive labels including an informative title that tells the story, descriptive subtitle explaining the pattern, and detailed caption with data source attribution

**Lines 74-104:** Multiple `annotate()` calls create a statistics summary box in the upper right corner containing:
- White rectangle background
- Title "Summary Statistics"
- Mean, median, standard deviation, and sample size
- Legend explaining the reference lines

**Lines 105-129:** Comprehensive theme customization including:
- Enhanced typography with specific sizes, weights, and colors for hierarchy
- Legend positioned at top
- Grid customization keeping only horizontal major gridlines
- Proper margins for professional spacing

::: {.highlight-box .success}
**Final result:**
A publication-ready histogram that clearly communicates the bimodal distribution of Old Faithful eruptions. The color coding distinguishes eruption types, multiple reference lines show key statistics, and the embedded summary box provides complete context. This chart is suitable for academic papers, reports, or presentations.

## Key Takeaways

::: {.callout-tip}
**Tips for Creating Better ggplot2 Histograms:**

1. **Choose bin width carefully** - Use the Freedman-Diaconis rule: `binwidth = 2 * IQR(x) / (length(x)^(1/3))` or experiment with different values to reveal patterns without over-smoothing

2. **Always specify binwidth or bins** - Never rely on ggplot2's default 30 bins; choose based on your data characteristics and the story you want to tell

3. **Add borders to bars** - Use `color = "white"` or `color = "gray30"` to define bar boundaries, especially important when bars are adjacent

4. **Consider density overlays** - Adding `geom_density()` scaled appropriately helps show the smoothed distribution pattern

5. **Show reference statistics** - Add vertical lines for mean, median, or other important values to provide context

6. **Use color meaningfully** - Color-code bins when there are natural categories or thresholds in your data

7. **Mind the y-axis** - Label as "Frequency", "Count", or "Number of Observations" rather than just "count" for clarity

8. **Handle skewed data** - For right-skewed distributions, consider log-transforming the x-axis with `scale_x_log10()`

9. **Annotate sample size** - Always show the total number of observations either in the subtitle or as an annotation

10. **Export at high resolution** - Use `ggsave("plot.png", width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)` for publication-quality images

:::

## Next Steps

Try applying these principles to other frequency visualizations:

- **Density plots** for smooth distribution curves without binning artifacts
- **Frequency polygons** (`geom_freqpoly()`) for comparing multiple groups
- **Ridgeline plots** for comparing distributions across many categories
- **Cumulative histograms** showing cumulative frequencies

::: {.highlight-box .info}
**Want to create comparative histograms?**

You can compare distributions across groups using facets or overlays:

```r
# Faceted approach (recommended for many groups)
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 500, fill = "#2C5F8D", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ cut, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Diamond Price Distribution by Cut Quality",
       x = "Price (USD)",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

# Overlay approach (best for 2-3 groups)
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = price, fill = cut)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 500, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme_minimal()
```
:::
